latest_release.name: Ray-2.60.1
latest_release.body:
# Security fixes

## brotli

- **CVE-2026-111497** (GHSA-9v8h-qqgm-4m35): an out-of-bounds write in the Brotli decoder in `brotli` 1.0.3 through 1.2.0, fixed in 1.2.1. It is listed in CISA KEV.  
- **Python requirements:** `brotli`, which Ray gets through `gradio`, moves to 1.2.1 in the compiled requirements and in the image, CI and release lock files. Ray's security requirements now set a `brotli>=1.2.1` floor (\#67789, pick \#67998).  
- **Docker images:** the Miniforge base environment in `base-deps` and `base-slim` shipped `brotli-python` 1.1.0, which no pip lock managed, so every `ray`, `ray-ml` and `ray-llm` image carried the vulnerable decoder. The images now install `brotli-python>=1.2.1` from conda on Python 3.11+, and `Brotli==1.2.1` from PyPI on Python 3.10 (\#67596, pick \#67997).

## ray (token authentication)

- **Group- or world-readable auth token file:** `ray.init()` starting a new local cluster with token authentication, and `ray get-auth-token --generate`, wrote the cluster auth token to `~/.ray/auth_token` with the default umask (typically `0644`), so other local users could read it.  
- Ray now creates the token file as `0600` and a new `~/.ray` directory as `0700` (\#66581, pick \#67993). A token file created by an earlier version keeps its permissions; run `chmod 600 ~/.ray/auth_token` to restrict it.

# Bug fixes

## Ray Data

- Reject column-mapped Delta tables in `read_delta` and `write_delta`, which silently produced null columns (\#67895, \#67898, picks \#68213, \#68231)  
- Return `None` for null tensor rows instead of another row's value or an error, and merge them across blocks (\#67579, \#67806, picks \#67999, \#68019; closes \#67200)  
- Stop writing Unity Catalog vended AWS credentials to the environment, where they replaced the job's own AWS identity and broke writes to its other buckets with `ACCESS_DENIED`. AWS Parquet reads through Unity Catalog now require `region` (\#67899, pick \#68232)  
- Keep every element of nested-null columns, such as `list<null>`, in Arrow-backed `to_pandas()`, which dropped elements or raised `ArrowInvalid` (\#67566, pick \#67994)  
- Fix a `TypeError` when a nested field is null in one block and a struct in another, and keep list types when unifying with `null` (\#66521, pick \#67995)  
- Take `read_delta` file sizes from the Delta log instead of making one `get_file_info` request per file, and add `partition_filters` to read only matching partitions (\#67900, pick \#68214)

## Ray Core

- Fix a spurious `RecursionError` that crashed async actor workers on Python 3.14 (\#67132, pick \#67996; closes \#66399)

# Thanks

Many thanks to all those who contributed to this release\!

@ronaldosaheki, @MortalHappiness, @sai-miduthuri, @abhishekverma-ray, @rayo5o, @elliot-barn, @dragongu, @marwan116, @Kunchd

Ray is a unified framework for scaling AI and Python applications. Ray consists of a core distributed runtime and a set of AI libraries for simplifying ML compute:

![](https://github.com/ray-project/ray/raw/master/doc/source/images/what-is-ray-padded.svg)

<!-- https://docs.google.com/drawings/d/1Pl8aCYOsZCo61cmp57c7Sja6HhIygGCvSZLi_AuBuqo/edit -->

Learn more about [Ray AI Libraries](https://docs.ray.io/en/latest/ray-air/getting-started.html):

- [Data](https://docs.ray.io/en/latest/data/data.html): Scalable Datasets for ML
- [Train](https://docs.ray.io/en/latest/train/train.html): Distributed Training
- [Tune](https://docs.ray.io/en/latest/tune/index.html): Scalable Hyperparameter Tuning
- [RLlib](https://docs.ray.io/en/latest/rllib/index.html): Scalable Reinforcement Learning
- [Serve](https://docs.ray.io/en/latest/serve/index.html): Scalable and Programmable Serving

Or more about [Ray Core](https://docs.ray.io/en/latest/ray-core/walkthrough.html) and its key abstractions:

- [Tasks](https://docs.ray.io/en/latest/ray-core/tasks.html): Stateless functions executed in the cluster.
- [Actors](https://docs.ray.io/en/latest/ray-core/actors.html): Stateful worker processes created in the cluster.
- [Objects](https://docs.ray.io/en/latest/ray-core/objects.html): Immutable values accessible across the cluster.

Learn more about Monitoring and Debugging:

- Monitor Ray apps and clusters with the [Ray Dashboard](https://docs.ray.io/en/latest/ray-core/ray-dashboard.html).
- Debug Ray apps with the [Ray Distributed Debugger](https://docs.ray.io/en/latest/ray-observability/ray-distributed-debugger.html).

Ray runs on any machine, cluster, cloud provider, and Kubernetes, and features a growing
[ecosystem of community integrations](https://docs.ray.io/en/latest/ray-overview/ray-libraries.html).

Install Ray with: `pip install ray`. For nightly wheels, see the
[Installation page](https://docs.ray.io/en/latest/ray-overview/installation.html).

## Why Ray?

Today's ML workloads are increasingly compute-intensive. As convenient as they are, single-node development environments such as your laptop cannot scale to meet these demands.

Ray is a unified way to scale Python and AI applications from a laptop to a cluster.

With Ray, you can seamlessly scale the same code from a laptop to a cluster. Ray is designed to be general-purpose, meaning that it can performantly run any kind of workload. If your application is written in Python, you can scale it with Ray, no other infrastructure required.
